metadata.note: The Aberdeen and Rockfish Railroad (organized 1892, John Blue of Aberdeen; never leased or merged, still Blue-family owned and today a freight short line) ran from the Seaboard Air Line at Aberdeen east through Raeford to Rockfish, then to Hope Mills on the ACL (1905-1912) and, from 23 Dec 1912, to Fayetteville. Passenger service: steam passenger train plus opposite mixed 1912-c.1921, then the gasoline rail motor 'jitney' to 1949/50. Drawn: the main line 1912-1949 and the pre-1912 Aberdeen - Hope Mills line as a 1905 [ANCHOR]. One company throughout, so no Rule 4 split.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue, Aberdeen and Rockfish entry (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. The live A&R freight line is tagged old_railway_operator='Aberdeen and Rockfish' / operator='Aberdeen and Rockfish Railroad' in OSM (ways 16487926, 1119068252, 428889124, 428889123, 657324142, 657324145, 318978814, 318978820, 657395246, 657395252, 318978817, 318978813); the Aberdeen - Fayetteville trace ran 43.3 mi on those ways and 0 mi on any other operator, with no straight legs. Waypoints: Aberdeen (west end of OSM way 16487926 at the SAL/CSX junction), Ashley Heights (Nominatim, statistical place), Raeford (Nominatim, town), Rockfish (Nominatim, statistical place), Fenix, Skibo (Nominatim hamlets), and the A&R's crossing of the ACL (CSX South End Subdivision) south of downtown Fayetteville (-78.8894, 35.0426). Every waypoint is within 0.3 km of the drawn line; check points Montrose, Timberland and Arabia lie within 0.03 km and Dundarrach 0.6 km. Juniper geocoded to a hamlet in Wake County (wrong place) and Endon did not geocode at all; neither was used. OSM rail-trail/abandoned ways and OpenHistoricalMap were queried for the Rockfish - Hope Mills and Ashley Heights - Endon areas and returned nothing for either A&R line (OHM has only the CF&YV, Chatham, Pinehurst and Aberdeen & Star roads there).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [ANCHOR] Aberdeen - Hope Mills drawn for 1905 only (Fowler 1905G); passenger years 1897-1904 and 1906-1911 on the pre-1912 line are unproven, not absent - a 1906-1911 timetable would let it join the 1912 main line. (2) Passenger end 1949 (Lewis 1991) vs 1950 (company, NC DNCR, Railway Age) vs 1951 (HawkinsRails, contradicted by the Feb 1952 Guide); a Raeford or Fayetteville newspaper story on the jitney's last run, or an NCUC discontinuance order, would settle it. (3) Steam-to-jitney changeover dated only to c. late 1921; whether the Fayetteville-originating mixed survived it is unknown. All headways and speeds are estimates. (4) The A&R's Fayetteville passenger depot was not located; the main line is cut at the ACL crossing. (5) Hope Mills Junction - Hope Mills grade: location and length (~7-9 mi) not established; drawn as a 6.5 mi straight line.
metadata.omitted: [3] Endon Branch (Aberdeen/Ashley Heights - Endon - Juniper, c.8 mi, 1895-1912; 1902 [ANCHOR] per Fowler 1902G): NOT DRAWN - Endon and Juniper could not be located (Endon does not geocode; 'Juniper' resolves to a Wake County hamlet), the area is now inside Fort Bragg, and neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap holds the grade; the report says omit rather than straight-line guess. For the same reason the 1902 anchor is not drawn on the shared Aberdeen - Ashley Heights stretch either. [4] Wagram Branch (Raeford - Wagram, 12 mi): NOT DRAWN - its only passenger evidence is one truncated sentence of the company history (implying 1913); opening date (1909 vs 1912) and the direction of the A&R / Laurinburg & Southern transfer conflict; report recommends omitting until a timetable is found. [5] Rockfish - Fenix 1904-1911: no passenger evidence before it became part of the through line in Dec 1912; drawn only from 1912 within the main line. [6] Fort Bragg troop specials after 1949 ('through the 1960s'): no dated run; main line not extended past 1949. [7] Old North State Chapter NRHS excursion, one weekend of October 1981: route not stated, and a full slider year for one weekend over-asserts; omitted per the report.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Main line after 1949; 1934 Cape Fear River terminal extension in Fayetteville; Skibo yard and industrial spurs; pre-1912 unnamed logging spurs; Laurinburg & Southern (incl. the ex-A&R Wagram line after 1921). Rule 1.

properties.geometry_quality: Aberdeen - Fayetteville: traced 43.3 mi against a documented 45 mi (Fowler's mileposts, Aberdeen 0 - Fayetteville 45) and 47 mi (Wikipedia / HawkinsRails / company: present route mileage, which may include Fayetteville terminal trackage) - 3.8% and 7.9% short. Traced chainage at the stations vs Fowler: Ashley Heights 5.2/5, Montrose 9.1/10, Timberland 13.2/15, Raeford 16.8/19 (town-centre geocode), Dundarrach 22.9/24, Arabia 25.1/26, Rockfish 29.5/30, Fenix 32.9/34, Skibo 38.4/40, end 43.3/45. No approximated (straight-line) legs. FAYETTEVILLE END: the line stops at the A&R's crossing of the Atlantic Coast Line south of downtown, about 1.3 km SSW of the ACL Hay Street station; the A&R's own Fayetteville passenger depot (photographed, NCSU Libraries bh2197pnc002/003) was not located, so the last ~1-2 mi to it are probably undrawn, which would explain much of the shortfall against Fowler's 45. The 1934 Cape Fear River terminal extension east of the ACL (OSM way 16511980, freight) and the A&R's present-day Fayetteville industrial spurs are deliberately NOT drawn (Rule 1). ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the alignment as OSM maps it today (the live freight line); any 1912-1949 line changes, the 1926 Skibo connection with the Army's Cape Fear Railway and the 1940 Skibo yard are not represented, and the line is not known to have been relocated, but this was not checked.

segments.note: Through passenger service Aberdeen - Ashley Heights - Raeford - Dundarrach - Rockfish - Fenix - Skibo - Fayetteville from 23 Dec 1912, the day the Fenix - Fayetteville extension opened ('The first train, a passenger run on December 23, 1912, reached Fayetteville with John Blue on board' - company history, Expansion & Redirection). Service: a daily passenger train out of Aberdeen in the morning, to Fayetteville at midday and back in the evening, plus a mixed train out of Fayetteville on the opposite schedule; no Sunday trains (Blue family rule). Ends c. late 1921, when 'to trim costs, the A&R did away with its passenger service, substituting a rail motor bus known locally as the jitney' (company history, Hard Times). headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE from that description (about two trips each way a day counting the mixed), not a timetable figure.
sources: Segment-level: start 23 Dec 1912 and the 1912-c.1921 service pattern from the A&R company history (Expansion & Redirection; Hard Times), adapted from Wrinn & Lewis, 'The Road of Personal Service' (1992); the c.1921 changeover year also per NC DNCR 2016 -- as quoted in research/branches/aberdeen_and_rockfish_railroad.txt (2026-11-04); the tracer did not re-open these pages.

segments.note: Rail passenger service by the gasoline rail motor 'jitney' (company: 'rail motor bus'; Railway Age 2017: 'gas-powered railbus'; pictured as the mail-and-passenger doodlebug in Beebe, Mixed Train Daily, 1947) - a rail car on A&R track, so passenger rail under Rule 1. WWII troop trains to Fort Bragg ran via the Skibo connection inside this span. END 1949: Lewis, American Shortline Railway Guide (1991) p.9 via Wikipedia and CRHA Carolina Conductor (May 2020) say passenger service ended in 1949; the company history, NC DNCR (2016) and Railway Age (2017) say the jitney was retired in 1950; HawkinsRails' 1951 is contradicted by the Feb 1952 Official Guide ('Regular passenger train service not operated'; SAL interline passengers carried by highway bus). Drawn to 1949, the year all sources agree passengers rode; 1950 is defensible but not drawn. Post-1950 Fort Bragg troop specials ('through the 1960s') are undated and not drawn. Freight continues today. headway_min 1440 (one round trip a day) is an ESTIMATE; the jitney's frequency is not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: end 1949 from Lewis 1991 p.9 as cited by Wikipedia (1950 per the company history and NC DNCR - conflict recorded in the note); jitney from the company history (Hard Times, Peace & Diesels); 1951 rejected against the Feb 1952 Official Guide A&R entry (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt ~line 123175, checked by the tracer) -- as quoted in research/branches/aberdeen_and_rockfish_railroad.txt (2026-11-04); the tracer did not re-open these pages.

properties.geometry_quality: Aberdeen - Hope Mills: 37.0 mi drawn. Aberdeen - Hope Mills Junction 30.5 mi traced on present-day A&R track (Fowler: Hope Mills Junction MP 31). Hope Mills Junction is not mapped anywhere; it is PLACED by chainage 1 mi beyond Rockfish on the present Rockfish - Fenix line (Fowler: Rockfish MP 30, Hope Mills Jct MP 31), at (-79.058287, 34.998736) - approximate. APPROXIMATED LEG: Hope Mills Junction - Hope Mills is a STRAIGHT LINE of 6.5 mi; the A&R grade (lifted after the Dec 1912 opening of the Fayetteville line) was not found in OSM rail-trail/abandoned data or OpenHistoricalMap. Its documented length is not established (~7-9 mi; Fowler prints Hope Mills as '40.', which would make it ~9 mi from MP 31). ERA CAVEAT: the Aberdeen - Rockfish part is drawn on today's alignment, a later layout than 1905; whether the 1905 line followed it exactly, and exactly where the Hope Mills line left it, is not established.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year. From 1905 to 1912 Aberdeen - Ashley Heights - Raeford - Dundarrach - Rockfish - Hope Mills Junction - Hope Mills (connection with the ACL) was the A&R main line (Wikipedia; construction: Raeford 1897/98, Dundarrach 1900/01, Rockfish 1902, Hope Mills 1905 - company history 'One Hundred Years Ago'). The only dated passenger evidence for this era is Fowler's listing 'Hope Mills (A&R later ACL 2nd) 1905G', i.e. the station appears on the A&R in the 1905 Official Guide. Service certainly ran wider both ways but no other year is confirmed: do NOT widen this anchor or bridge 1906-1911 to the 1912 start of the Aberdeen - Fayetteville feature without a timetable. The Rockfish - Hope Mills line was abandoned on completion of the Fayetteville line in Dec 1912 (company history, Expansion & Redirection). headway_min 1440 is a placeholder ESTIMATE (one train a day); frequency and whether trains were mixed are not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1905 from Fowler, North Carolina railroads file table 74 ('Hope Mills ... 1905G'), as read in research/branches/aberdeen_and_rockfish_railroad.txt (2026-11-04); the tracer did not open the PDF. Headway not sourced.
